subject: Rate alignment & technical carveout proposal for BrightLoop
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Rate alignment & technical carveout proposal for BrightLoop

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

BrightLoop came back after the demo with an ask: they want a single blended rate that matches (or slightly undercuts) their incumbent, Megajoule AI, and a short-term migration credit to cover integration effort. They also raised concerns about a specific runtime behavior they rely on (persistent KV cache semantics across warm restarts) — the customer calls it a "technical carveout": if we can't guarantee parity there, they'll demand a larger credit.

Key context:
- ACV ask: ~$1.1M committed over 12 months (usage-heavy inference, bursty peaks).
- Incumbent rate they quoted: $0.0045 per token (they claim).
- BrightLoop wants a 3-month migration credit and an SLA uplift during onboarding.

Can you outline 2-3 packaging/pricing options we can present — one aggressive match, one conservative (higher price, smaller credit), and any non-priced concessions (SLA, ramp milestones, performance trial). Also note any absolute deal breakers for the engineering team re: the KV cache expectation.

I attached the quick TCO model they sent (BrightLoop_TCO_model.xlsx).

Thanks,
Jonas
Account Executive — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 May 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rate alignment & technical carveout proposal for BrightLoop

Jonas —

Thanks for the summary. High-level options below; I left room for composition (commits + one-time credits + SLA add-on). Notes on feasibility follow.

Option A (Aggressive - match incumbent)
- Pricing: $0.0044 per token equivalent for first 12 months
- Commitment: $1.1M ACV guaranteed
- Migration: One-time credit equal to 10% of committed ACV (applied as token credits over first 90 days)
- SLA: 99.9% onboarding SLA with a 30-day performance pilot (no extra cost)
- Conditions: Engineering sign-off that the KV cache gap can be mitigated with a short-term adapter (see feasibility notes)

Option B (Balanced)
- Pricing: $0.0050 per token equivalent, with 5% effective rebate if usage > 120% of forecast in first 6 months
- Commitment: $1.1M ACV
- Migration: $50k one-time credit
- SLA: standard SLA; onboarding support included
- Conditions: If KV cache parity proves critical, increase migration credit by up to $25k to cover engineering time

Option C (Conservative)
- Pricing: $0.0055 per token equivalent
- Commitment: Minimum $900k ACV (lower commitment)
- Migration: $25k credit
- SLA: standard

Engineering feasibility (KV cache):
- Our runtime supports KV caching, but not the exact sticky persistence semantics across host restarts that Megajoule advertises. We can create a short-term shim that preserves the KV layer across warm restarts for the pilot, but it will add ~4–6 weeks of engineering effort and an operational risk.
- If BrightLoop treats that as mandatory parity, we should push more migration credit or a staggered rollout (pilot -> partial production -> full cutover).

Deal guardrails:
- Max concession ceiling: 12% of ACV in aggregate concessions without exec approval.
- Any multi-quarter credit or rebate beyond 15% requires VP Sales approval.

If you want to be aggressive on A, I recommend a capped proposal: A + capped migration credit of $110k and a conditional engineering commitment (pilot shim for 90 days, then revisit).

-Karthik
Head of Commercial Strategy

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Bennett <sarah@brightloop.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, BrightLoop Procurement <procurement@brightloop.com>
Date: Wed, 2 May 2028 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood proposal — performance-aligned options for BrightLoop (DL-2028-BL-917)

Hi Sarah —

Great talking yesterday. Per our discussion, attached is a short hand summary of three commercial options we can offer. High level:

- Option A (match): $0.0044 / token equivalent; $1.1M ACV; 10% one-time migration credit (token credit delivered over first 90 days); onboarding pilot; conditional technical shim to preserve KV cache behavior for the pilot window.
- Option B (balanced): $0.0050 / token equivalent; $1.1M ACV; $50k migration credit; standard SLA; performance rebate if usage exceeds forecast.
- Option C (conservative): $0.0055 / token equivalent; $900k ACV minimum; $25k migration credit.

We can include a 30-day performance pilot (no additional charge) and an SLA uplift during onboarding for Option A. The aggressive match is contingent on our engineering team delivering the shim for the KV cache for the pilot period — we estimate a 4–6 week delivery window for that work and would like to limit the shim to the pilot (technical parity for full production would be a roadmap conversation).

Attachments: BrightLoop_TCO_model.xlsx (your model), and a short proposal summary hosted here: https://docs.redwood.com/shared/brightloop-proposal-v1

If you prefer, we can prepare a one-page redline for SLAs/credits and circulate for countersignature. Let me know which option you want to pursue; if it's Option A, I will request a capped migration credit sign-off from Sales Ops.

Best,
Jonas

From: Sarah Bennett <sarah@brightloop.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightLoop Procurement <procurement@brightloop.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 May 2028 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal — performance-aligned options for BrightLoop (DL-2028-BL-917)

Jonas —

Thanks for the options. A few clarifications and our counter:

1) The KV cache parity is non-negotiable for the first calendar quarter post-cutover. Our production pipelines rely on cross-batch state being available without rehydration delays. A pilot shim is acceptable, but we need a path to production parity within 90 days after cutover.

2) We'd like Option A structure but ask to shift the migration credit from a token credit to a direct $90k credit applied to the first invoice. That helps our finance team with short-term cashflow.

3) SLA: we expect an uptime SLA of 99.95% for the first 6 months post-cutover and a financial remedy tier (credits) for any missed SLOs during that period.

4) Finally, given the incumbent's complexity, we request a 45-day rollback clause that allows us to revert traffic to Megajoule with a pro-rated credit if the production rollout hits an unresolved perf/regression.

If you can accept the above, we are ready to put this on the procurement calendar for signatures.

Best,
Sarah Bennett
VP Finance — BrightLoop

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 May 2028 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Redwood proposal — performance-aligned options for BrightLoop (DL-2028-BL-917)

Forwarding Sarah's counters. Highlights: they want the KV parity within 90 days post-cutover (production), migration credit as $90k invoice credit, SLA 99.95% for 6 months with financial remedies, and a 45-day rollback clause.

Can we structure a final internal approval path? Per Karthik's earlier memo our concession ceiling is 12% of ACV without exec sign-off — the $90k on a $1.1M ACV is ~8.2%, so in-range. The SLA uplift and rollback clause are risk items. We need:

- Marissa: commercial OK on the $90k invoice credit and the conditional rollback clause?
- Karthik: do we accept the 99.95% onboarding SLA with credits? If yes, what cap on credits (percent of ACV) do we set?
- Also confirm engineering timeline for production-grade KV parity (90 days after cutover).

Jonas

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 May 2028 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Redwood proposal — performance-aligned options for BrightLoop (DL-2028-BL-917)

Team —

I reviewed the counters with Sales Ops and Legal. Approve moving forward with the customer's requested structure with these firm limits: 

1) Migration concession: $90,000 invoice credit (one-time) — approved.
2) SLA: 99.95% for first 6 months post-cutover with financial credits capped at 5% of ACV (applied quarterly).
3) Rollback clause: 45-day rollback window is acceptable but must include a joint runbook and predefined criteria for rollback triggers (performance, error budget exhaustion).
4) Engineering commitment: we'll deliver the pilot shim as discussed; production parity (no shim) must be on our roadmap within 90 days post-cutover. Engineering has preliminarily confirmed feasibility but requires a small budget holdback for unplanned edge cases.

Attached: SLA_redline_BrightLoop_v2.pdf (legal redline including the credit cap and rollback runbook summary). Please work with Legal to finalize language and prepare a one-page amendment. Jon, loop in the engineering lead for the 90-day parity plan and request a signed commitment in the SOW.

Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
